import pytest
from target import url_basename

# Expected behavior based on the OLD implementation
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url,expected",
    [
        # Simple cases
        ("http://example.com/foo", "foo"),
        ("https://example.com/foo", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo?bar=baz", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo#section", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/?bar=baz", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/#section", "foo"),
        # Multiple path segments – should return the last segment
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c", "c"),
        ("https://example.com/one/two/three/", "three"),
        ("http://example.com/one/two/three?x=1", "three"),
        ("http://example.com/one/two/three#frag", "three"),
        # Empty input
        ("", ""),
        # No path after domain
        ("http://example.com", ""),
        ("https://example.com/", ""),
        # Path that ends with a slash but has no basename
        ("http://example.com//", ""),
        # Path with only query/fragment after domain
        ("http://example.com?query=1", ""),
        ("http://example.com#frag", ""),
        # URL with port number
        ("http://example.com:8080/foo", "foo"),
        # URL with userinfo
        ("http://user:pass@example.com/foo", "foo"),
        # URL with IPv6 host
        ("http://[2001:db8::1]/foo", "foo"),
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_expected_behavior(url, expected):
    assert url_basename(url) == expected


def test_regression_multiple_segments():
    """
    The change introduced a stricter regex that may fail on URLs with
    more than two path segments. This test ensures the function still
    returns the last segment for such URLs.
    """
    url = "http://example.com/segment1/segment2/segment3"
    assert url_basename(url) == "segment3"


def test_edge_cases():
    # Zero-length string
    assert url_basename("") == ""

    # Single slash after domain (no basename)
    assert url_basename("http://example.com/") == ""

    # Trailing slash after basename
    assert url_basename("http://example.com/basename/") == "basename"

    # Query string without basename
    assert url_basename("http://example.com/?q=1") == ""

    # Fragment without basename
    assert url_basename("http://example.com/#frag") == ""

    # Path containing characters that were previously allowed in the optional segment
    # (e.g., additional slashes). The function should still capture the final segment.
    assert url_basename("http://example.com/a/b/c/d") == "d"
